subject: Operations
title: Labor Standards Worldwide
description: A 60-second lesson on Labor Standards Worldwide.

hook.text: A factory in Country A pays workers $2/day with 14-hour shifts. In Country B, that's illegal. Who sets the standard?

buildup.text: Labor standards vary wildly: minimum wage, working hours, child labor laws, and safety regulations differ by country.

discovery.text: The ILO sets international labor standards, but enforcement depends entirely on national governments.

twist.text: Companies sourcing from low-standard countries face reputational risk even if they follow local laws.

climax.text: Nike's 1990s sweatshop scandal showed that customers hold brands responsible for supplier labor practices.

punchline.text: Legal doesn't mean ethical. The market judges both.
